models.name: M1-one-family
models.conclusion: E1 holds while E2 fails: the existential form does not imply the family-invariance form
models.reading_source: toy model; the paper-side analogue is N03 O1 vs O5

models.name: M2-two-families
models.conclusion: each family is satisfiable on its own and the joint constraint is satisfiable here, so this model does NOT exhibit the failure; it is the control case. The failure is M2b below.
models.reading_source: toy model; paper-side analogue: two requirements sharing one S (N07 W9)

models.name: M2b-two-families-disjoint
models.conclusion: both families are individually satisfiable and jointly unsatisfiable: "there is an S for each requirement" does not give "there is one S for both"
models.reading_source: toy model; this is the smallest instance of the joint-witness fallacy named in N07

models.name: M3-unknown-relation
models.conclusion: the extra assumption removes the assignments with x = y = 1 that satisfy every known constraint, i.e. assuming independence narrows the model without evidence; unknown relations must be reported as UNKNOWN, not silently closed
models.reading_source: catalog N10 instruction: missing relations must stay unknown

scope_note: every verdict is an exhaustive enumeration over the named finite model; finite unsatisfiability is not a statement about IUT
